history.recommendation_text: The Board recommends that, subject to the legal framework, the Administration better track recoveries that were identified in the recommendations of the Office of Internal Oversight Services.
history.administration_response: The Organization has taken steps to coordinate a review of the end-to-end process, including mechanisms for quantifying losses and updating the guidelines on fraud and presumptive fraud. With regard to the implementation of a mechanism to track recoveries, the Administration emphasizes that case investigations and recoveries are monitored at the entity level, in line with the delegation of authority framework, with heads of entities being accountable as the first line of defence. However, the Administration recognizes the need for a mechanism to track recoveries at the corporate level. To enable corporate-level tracking, beyond the annual information- gathering exercise conducted by the Office of Programme Planning, Finance and Budget, additional capacity would be required to establish a dedicated unit for managing fraud risks, including recovery tracking and the development of a centralized platform to consolidate cases, enabling efficient monitoring and reporting. This initiative would increase the workload of the Financial Policy and Internal Controls Service, which is already responsible for compiling annual fraud case data. Additional resources would need to be budgeted and approved to support its implementation. In the light of the current liquidity constraints and recent progress on process improvements, the Administration proposes that the recommendation be closed.
history.board_assessment: Given that the Office of Human Resources, together with the Office of Programme Planning, Finance and Budget, will coordinate with relevant stakeholders and closely collaborate with OIOS to carry out the relevant work, the Board considers the recommendation to be under implementation.
